title: Cảm Xúc Là Kẻ Thù Số Một Của Thành Công
author: TS. Lê Thẩm Dương (compiled/ghostwritten by journalist Nguyễn Tuấn Anh)
summary:
Cảm Xúc Là Kẻ Thù Số Một Của Thành Công ("Emotion Is the Number One Enemy of Success") is a Vietnamese-market self-help book compiled from the talks, lectures, and interviews of Dr. Lê Thẩm Dương, a well-known Vietnamese business lecturer and head of the Business Administration faculty at the Banking University of Ho Chi Minh City. Rather than being written as a single continuous narrative, the book is assembled — credited in later editions to journalist Nguyễn Tuấn Anh as the writer who shaped Dương's spoken material into book form — from material Dương delivered across numerous public talks and media appearances aimed primarily at a young adult audience.

The book's central thesis, reflected directly in its title, is that emotional volatility, more than lack of skill or opportunity, is what most often derails people on the path to success — whether that shows up as impatience, defensiveness, romantic decision-making driven by comparison and insecurity, or an inability to separate feeling from judgment in professional and financial decisions. Dương's material draws heavily on concrete, often provocative real-life framings rather than abstract theory; one widely referenced example reframes unemployment not as a personal failure but as, in his words, a natural and even healthy signal of a functioning market economy, intended to reduce the emotional weight readers attach to job loss.

Because the book compiles talks delivered over time rather than being written sequentially as chapters, its structure is looser and more thematic than a typical single-author business book — reader reviews describe it as somewhat disjointed between individual pieces of advice, even as they credit the overall collection with genuine practical value. Successive editions of the book (2016 through a 2021 revised edition) have varied somewhat in exactly which talks and topics are included, with the 2021 edition specifically adding expanded material on personal financial management, reflecting Dương's growing emphasis on that topic in his more recent public talks. A separate sequel, Cảm Xúc Là Kẻ Thù Số Một Của Thành Công 2, published in 2019, extends the same format with additional talks not included in the original.

The book's overall throughline is that emotional self-management is a learnable, practical skill rather than an innate personality trait — and that mastering it, more than any specific tactical business or life advice, is what actually separates people who achieve their goals from those who don't.

sections.title: Emotion and Personal Life Decisions
sections.summary:
This thematic group of the book's compiled talks addresses how uncontrolled emotion distorts personal and relationship decisions, most notably around choosing a spouse or partner. It works from the premise that many people make life-partner decisions based on comparison, insecurity, or momentary emotional states rather than clear-eyed judgment.

The material in this section includes Dương's widely referenced framing of choosing a spouse "by function or by variable" (hàm số hay biến số) — arguing that a stable, well-chosen partner functions like a dependable mathematical function producing consistent results, while an emotionally driven choice behaves more like an unpredictable variable — used as a memorable device for encouraging readers to evaluate relationship decisions more deliberately.

This section connects to the following one by extending the same core argument — that unmanaged emotion distorts judgment — from personal relationships into professional and economic decision-making.
keyLessons: Major personal decisions, including choosing a life partner, are frequently distorted by comparison and momentary emotion rather than clear judgment.
Using deliberate frameworks or metaphors (like Dương's "function versus variable" comparison) can help separate emotional reaction from considered decision-making.
Emotional self-awareness in personal relationships is presented as a skill directly transferable to professional decision-making.

sections.title: Emotion, Work, and Economic Setbacks
sections.summary:
This thematic group applies the book's core argument to professional and economic circumstances, most notably reframing job loss and unemployment as a normal feature of a functioning market economy rather than a personal failure warranting emotional collapse. It opens from the observation that many people attach outsized shame and anxiety to career setbacks.

The material here includes Dương's frequently cited framing that unemployment is, in a market economy, "a wonderful signal" of healthy economic churn rather than evidence of personal inadequacy — intended to help readers separate the emotional weight of a job loss from its actual practical implications, freeing them to respond strategically rather than reactively.

This section hands off to the book's later, expanded material (particularly in the 2021 edition) on personal financial management, extending the theme of emotional regulation into the specific domain of money management.
keyLessons: Reframing job loss as a normal feature of a dynamic market economy, rather than personal failure, is presented as reducing unproductive shame and anxiety.
Separating the emotional response to a setback from its practical implications allows for a more strategic response.
The book treats economic and career setbacks as a specific, recurring test case for the broader skill of emotional regulation.

sections.title: Personal Financial Management
sections.summary:
Added most substantially in the book's 2021 revised edition, this thematic group addresses personal finance directly, reflecting what Dương has described as an area he became increasingly focused on given the economic pressures of the period in which the revised edition was prepared. It connects financial decision-making back to the book's central emotional-regulation thesis.

The material in this section addresses managing personal finances with the same emotional discipline advocated throughout the rest of the book, treating financial anxiety and impulsive financial decision-making as further specific instances of the general pattern the book is organized around: emotion overriding sound judgment.
keyLessons: Personal financial decisions are treated as another domain where unmanaged emotion — anxiety, impulsiveness — undermines sound judgment.
The book connects financial discipline directly back to its central thesis about emotional self-management rather than treating it as a separate topic.
This section was added or substantially expanded in later editions, reflecting the book's ongoing revision in response to changing economic conditions.
Unmanaged emotion, more than lack of skill or opportunity, is presented as the most common thing standing between people and their goals.
Major life decisions, including choosing a partner, benefit from deliberately separating emotional reaction from considered judgment.
Reframe job loss and economic setbacks as normal features of a dynamic market and economy, not as evidence of personal failure.
Treat financial decision-making as another domain requiring the same emotional discipline applied elsewhere in life.
Emotional self-regulation is presented throughout as a learnable, practical skill rather than a fixed personality trait.
Concrete, memorable reframings (like the "function versus variable" comparison) can help translate an abstract principle into an applicable decision tool.
Separating the emotional weight of a setback from its practical implications allows for a more strategic, less reactive response.
Because the book compiles talks delivered over time, readers may find it more useful to sample sections relevant to their current situation than to read straight through.

conceptsFrameworks.name: "Hàm Số Hay Biến Số" (Function or Variable)
conceptsFrameworks.definition: A metaphor, drawn from mathematics, that Dương uses to frame the choice of a life partner: a well-chosen, stable partner behaves like a dependable mathematical function that reliably produces consistent, predictable outcomes, while an emotionally or superficially driven choice behaves more like an unpredictable variable. The framework is used to argue for evaluating relationship decisions with the same deliberateness one might apply to any other major, consequential choice.

conceptsFrameworks.name: Emotion as "Enemy Number One"
conceptsFrameworks.definition: The book's core organizing claim, given directly in its title: that unmanaged emotional reaction, more consistently than any single external circumstance, is the primary obstacle standing between a person and their goals — applied throughout the book across personal relationships, career setbacks, and financial decisions as the same underlying pattern recurring in different domains.
conceptsFrameworks.sourceSection: throughout, stated most directly in the book's title and framing

actionSteps: Before making your next significant personal or financial decision, write down separately what you feel about the decision and what you factually know about it, and compare the two lists.

If you're currently dealing with a career setback, write one sentence reframing it as a normal, expected feature of a dynamic economy or industry, distinct from a statement about your own worth or competence.

Apply Dương's "function versus variable" framing to one current relationship or major personal decision: does this choice behave predictably and reliably, or is it more like an unpredictable variable you're hoping will stabilize?
Track your emotional state before making any financial decision this month above a threshold that matters to you, and note whether you were making the decision from a calm or an anxious/urgent state.
reflectionQuestions: Think of a recent decision — personal, professional, or financial — that you now regret. Was emotion, rather than a lack of information, the more significant factor?
Is there a career or financial setback you're currently carrying more personal shame about than the situation actually warrants?
Where in your life do you currently treat emotional reaction as identical to sound judgment, rather than as one input among several?

points: Because the book is compiled from spoken talks and interviews rather than written as a unified text, multiple reader reviews specifically describe it as disjointed or uneven between sections, which the book's own promotional material implicitly acknowledges by emphasizing its "philosophies" and standalone "lessons" rather than a continuous argument.

The book's central claims are presented largely through Dương's own rhetorical framing and personal experience as a lecturer, rather than through cited psychological or economic research, so readers looking for an evidence-based treatment of emotional regulation should treat this as motivational and experiential rather than empirically grounded.

The book exists in multiple, meaningfully different editions (2016 through 2021) with content added and removed between versions, which makes it important for a reader or reviewer to be clear about which specific edition they're referencing, since claims about "the book's" content may not hold consistently across editions.

Reports of the book being widely counterfeited in the Vietnamese market, cited by the author himself as partial motivation for the 2021 revised edition, raise the practical concern that not all copies in circulation reflect the author's actual intended content.

whoThisIsFor: A general Vietnamese young-adult audience, particularly readers navigating early career setbacks, relationship decisions, or general life direction who respond well to a direct, motivational speaking style.
whenToReadThis: Well suited to being read in shorter sessions around specific life moments — a career setback, a major relationship decision — rather than as a single continuous read.

authorBio.name: TS. Lê Thẩm Dương
authorBio.bio:
Dr. Lê Thẩm Dương is a Vietnamese academic and public speaker who serves as head of the Business Administration faculty at the Banking University of Ho Chi Minh City, and who has built a wide public following, particularly among younger Vietnamese audiences, through direct, often provocative public talks and media appearances on business, finance, and life skills.

Beyond his university role, Dương serves as a lead instructor for programs certifying finance professionals under Vietnam's State Securities Commission and is a frequently invited guest lecturer for corporations, universities, and training programs, as well as a regular guest on national television and at public forums. This book and its sequel are compiled from that body of public speaking work, credited to journalist Nguyễn Tuấn Anh as the writer who assembled Dương's spoken material into published form.

sourceNotes: Author identity and general framing verified across multiple independent Vietnamese-language sources (YBOX/Bookademy, VietnamNet, VOV.VN, and a personal review blog), which were consistent with each other on the book's compiled-talks structure, its core thesis, the "unemployment as market signal" and "function versus variable" examples, and the existence of multiple editions and a sequel. A full, formal chapter-by-chapter table of contents could not be located, consistent with the book's own described nature as a compilation of talks rather than a sequentially structured text; the three thematic groupings presented here reflect themes confirmed as present across multiple independent source descriptions, not a verified formal table of contents, and this is flagged honestly per the project's standing instruction. Quotes are drawn from short excerpts appearing consistently across multiple independent Vietnamese source articles describing the book's content.
